home.title: {voices, number} voices. One shelf.
home.sub: Speakshelf catalogs the text to speech voices of {names} and more. Each with a sample you can play in the browser. No account, no setup, just the voices.
home.providersSub: Every provider keeps a full shelf: the complete voice list with filters and playback, notes on each model family, and a page per language. The shelf grows: the AI TTS Microservice unifies more providers, and new shelves open here once verified.
home.cardMeta: {languages, plural, one {# language} other {# languages}} · {familiesCount} {familyWord} · {samples, plural, one {# sample} other {# samples}}
home.whySub: Catalogs differ in more than size. Keeping them side by side shows the gaps, the overlaps and the character of each.
home.why1GapAndVariants: Amazon Polly brings {gap}, which Google Cloud doesn't carry at all, plus regional variants like {v1} and {v2}. One shelf shows what each provider has that the others lack.
home.why1GapOnly: Amazon Polly brings {gap}, which Google Cloud doesn't carry at all. One shelf shows what each provider has that the others lack.
home.why1VariantsOnly: Amazon Polly adds regional variants like {v1} and {v2}. One shelf shows what each provider has that the others lack.
home.why1Generic: One shelf shows what each provider has that the others lack.
home.why2Body: Same filters, same player, same voice id scheme on every shelf. Comparing voices across providers is two clicks, not two consoles.
home.why3Body: Every shelf refreshes from the AI TTS Microservice daily. New voices, languages and sub-models appear here without anyone editing the site.
home.aboutBody: Speakshelf is a reference catalog for text to speech voices. Today it carries {voices, number} voices from {providers, plural, one {# provider} other {# providers}} in {languages, plural, one {# language} other {# languages}}, every one with a sample you can play. Voices are grouped the way their providers group them, into model families and engines, so what you hear maps onto what you would deploy.

attribution.independence: Speakshelf is independent and not affiliated with any provider it catalogs.
attribution.independenceNamed: Speakshelf is independent and not affiliated with {name}.
attribution.source: Voice data and audio come from the <link>AI TTS Microservice</link>, a service that unifies Google, Amazon, Azure and other speech providers behind a single endpoint. Samples stream on demand, so listening is free.

google.heroTitle: Every Google voice, on one page.
google.heroSub: Play a sample of every voice in the Google Cloud catalog. Filter by model family, language and gender. No account, no setup, just the voices.
google.familiesIntro: Google keeps shipping new speech architectures and every generation is still in service. The catalog runs from compact parametric voices to models you can direct with a sentence.
google.card: The deepest shelf here: model families from Standard and WaveNet to Chirp 3 and Gemini voices that follow a written style prompt.
google.about: Google Cloud runs one of the largest text to speech catalogs of any cloud provider. It spans {families, number} model families, from the WaveNet voices that made neural speech mainstream to Gemini voices that change their delivery when you describe the tone you want. Gemini is really {models, number} models in one: every Gemini voice can be rendered by any of its sub-models, and each render has its own sample here. Every other voice in the catalog has a sample too.
google.unknownFamily: A recent addition to the Google catalog.

polly.heroTitle: Every Amazon Polly voice, on one page.
polly.heroSub: Play a sample of every voice in the Amazon Polly catalog. Filter by engine, language and gender. No account, no setup, just the voices.
polly.familiesIntro: Polly groups its voices by engine. The catalog runs from the standard voices to the generative engine, with a long-form tier built for extended listening.
polly.card: AWS's text to speech service: standard, neural, generative and long-form engines.
polly.about: Amazon Polly is the text to speech service on AWS, converting text into lifelike speech. Its {voices, number} voices here span {families, number} engines: standard and neural, a generative engine built with generative AI techniques, and long-form voices designed for longer content like articles and training material. Every voice has a playable sample.
polly.unknownFamily: A recent addition to the Amazon Polly catalog.

kokoro.heroTitle: Every Kokoro voice, on one page.
kokoro.heroSub: Play a sample of every voice of the open-weight Kokoro model. Filter by language and gender. No account, no setup, just the voices.
kokoro.familiesIntro: Kokoro is a single model rather than a stable of engines, so its whole catalog sits in one family.
kokoro.card: An open-weight model, 82 million parameters under the Apache 2.0 license.
kokoro.about: Kokoro is an open-weight text to speech model: 82 million parameters, released under the Apache 2.0 license. The AI TTS Microservice serves it alongside the cloud catalogs, so its {voices, number} voices in {languages, number} languages play here like any other shelf. Every voice has a playable sample.
kokoro.unknownFamily: A recent addition to the Kokoro catalog.

providerPage.languagesSub: Every language has its own page with the full list of voices, so you can link someone straight to one shelf of the catalog.

Gemini.blurb: Native speech from Gemini. Each voice can be rendered by every sub-model, and delivery follows a written style prompt.
Gemini.note: Samples show each voice honestly, quirks included. Some Gemini voices can render a different accent than their locale label, an en-US voice sounding en-IN for instance. In your own generation prompt, a plain instruction like "say this in an American accent" usually corrects it.

Chirp3HD.blurb: The current HD generation, tuned for natural conversation.

Standard.blurb: Parametric voices with the widest language coverage at the lowest price.

Wavenet.blurb: The DeepMind model that made neural speech mainstream.

Neural2.blurb: Second generation neural voices, the default for many products.

ChirpHD.blurb: The first Chirp generation, still widely deployed.

News.blurb: Broadcast style voices tuned for reading the news.

Studio.blurb: Narration grade voices for long form reading.

Polyglot.blurb: One voice identity that speaks several languages.

Casual.blurb: A conversational voice built for informal replies.

Neural.blurb: Neural voices, the machine learning generation that lifted Polly's speech quality.

Standard.blurb: The standard engine, Polly's baseline voices with wide language coverage.

Generative.blurb: The newest Polly engine, built on generative AI for conversational speech.

LongForm.blurb: Made for long listening: articles, training material and narration.

Kokoro.blurb: Every Kokoro voice: one open-weight model, 82 million parameters, Apache 2.0.
